newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's February c/a deficit soars to $2.45 bln.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's February c/a deficit soars to $2.45 bln.

text.p: South Korea's current account deficit soared to $2.45 billion in February from $1.98 billion a year earlier, preliminary figures of the Bank of Korea (BOK) showed on Friday.
NOTE - Figures are in millions of US dollars
The deficit totalled $5.59 billion for the first two months of this year, against $3.70 billion a year before, the central bank said in a statement.
It said the widening deficit in February was due mostly to a continuing export slowdown. Free-on-board exports fell 4.3 percent year-on-year, while imports rose 0.6 percent.
Despite a slowdown in exports of electronics goods and automobiles, the February trade deficit narrowed from January as an economic downturn put a cap on import growth.
Electronics exports dropped 18.6 percent to $1.72 billion in February, compared with 28.6 percent growth to $2.12 billion a year earlier.
Slow semiconductor exports, as a result of weak global prices for dynamic random access memory chips, helped widen the trade deficit.
Letters of credit received in February dropped 10.1 percent to $4.89 billion from a year ago.

Customs-cleared imports of raw materials rose 2.1 percent in February, sharply less than growth of 22.1 percent a year earlier. Imports of food and consumer goods edged down 1.5 percent last month, compared with a 25.8 percent rise a year earlier.

Rises in travel and transport expenses were largely responsible for the $590.5 million invisible trade deficit. The travel deficit rose to $247.4 million in February from $116.8 million a year earlier, the central bank figures showed.
South Korea's Finance and Economy Ministry has forecast this year's current account deficit at about $18 billion, compared with a $23.72 billion shortfall in 1996.
